exercises.name: High-Bar Back Squat
instructions: Set the bar on top of the traps, grip as narrow as is comfortable, and pull the shoulder blades together.
Unrack, step back into your stance, take a big breath into the belly, and brace all the way around the trunk.
Bend the knees and hips together and sit straight down, keeping the torso fairly upright and the weight over the middle of the foot.
Go as deep as you can hold position, then drive up with the chest and hips rising at the same speed.
exercises.formCue: Sit down between your heels, chest tall.
exercises.commonMistakes: Letting the hips shoot up first out of the bottom, or losing the brace and folding forward.
exercises.beginnerModification: Squat to a box at parallel height with an empty bar, or use a goblet squat until the upright position feels natural.
exercises.whyThisMatters: The upright, deep position builds the quads and carries straight over to front squats and the Olympic lifts.

exercises.name: Low-Bar Back Squat
exercises.musclesWorked: Glutes, quads, hamstrings, adductors, spinal erectors
instructions: Set the bar a few centimetres below the top of the traps, across the rear shoulders, and squeeze the upper back tight to make a shelf.
Unrack, take two short steps back, breathe in, and brace hard.
Push the hips back as the knees bend and let the torso lean forward enough to keep the bar over the middle of the foot.
Lower until the hip crease drops just below the top of the knee.
Drive the hips and shoulders up together until you stand fully locked out.
exercises.formCue: Bar over midfoot, the whole way down and up.
exercises.commonMistakes: Bar rolling down the back because the upper back is loose, or cutting depth as the load gets heavy.
exercises.beginnerModification: Learn the bar position with an empty bar and squat to a box set just below parallel.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It is the bar position most powerlifters use because it lets the hips do more of the work.

exercises.name: Pause Squat
instructions: Set up and descend exactly as you would for your normal back squat.
Stop dead at the bottom and hold for two to three seconds with the trunk braced hard.
Stay still during the hold with no bouncing or rocking.
Drive straight up as fast as you can and stand fully before the next rep.
exercises.formCue: Stay tight in the hole, then explode.
exercises.commonMistakes: Cutting the pause short, or relaxing the trunk at the bottom and losing position.
exercises.beginnerModification: Use a lighter load with a one-second pause, or pause a goblet squat first.
exercises.whyThisMatters: Removing the bounce builds strength and control in the hardest part of the squat.

exercises.name: Pin Squat
exercises.equipment: Barbell, power rack with safety pins
instructions: Set the rack pins at the squat depth you want to train.
Lower under control until the bar settles completely on the pins.
Keep your position over the middle of the foot and brace the trunk again while the pins hold the weight.
Drive the bar off the pins and accelerate all the way to standing.
Let every rep come to a full stop on the pins before the next one.
exercises.formCue: Dead stop, get tight, then drive.
exercises.commonMistakes: Bouncing the bar off the pins, or relaxing so much on the pins that your position is lost.
exercises.beginnerModification: Set the pins a little higher and use a light load until you can settle and restart without shifting.
exercises.whyThisMatters: Starting from a dead stop teaches you to produce force with no rebound at your weakest depth.

exercises.name: Box Squat
exercises.equipment: Barbell, squat rack, box or bench
instructions: Place a sturdy box behind you at about parallel height and unrack the bar on your upper back.
Sit the hips back and down under control, keeping the shins close to vertical.
Settle onto the box lightly while staying braced, without dropping or rocking.
Drive through the whole foot and stand up until hips and knees are locked.
exercises.formCue: Sit back softly, stay tight on the box.
exercises.commonMistakes: Crashing onto the box, or relaxing the trunk while seated and rocking forward to get up.
exercises.beginnerModification: Use a higher box and a goblet hold, then lower the box as control improves.
exercises.whyThisMatters: The box gives the same depth every rep and loads the hips hard from a controlled stop.

exercises.name: Safety Bar Squat
exercises.musclesWorked: Quads, glutes, upper back, spinal erectors
instructions: Duck under the bar so the pad sits across the shoulders with the yoke around the neck, and hold the handles.
Unrack, step back, set your stance, and brace.
Bend the hips and knees and squat until the thighs are just past parallel, keeping the chest up against the forward pull of the bar.
Drive back up by extending the hips and knees until you are standing tall.
exercises.formCue: Chest up, do not let the bar fold you.
exercises.commonMistakes: Letting the upper back round forward, or pulling the handles down so the bar tips.
exercises.beginnerModification: Start light and squat to a box until you can hold the upright position.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It trains the squat hard while asking far less of the shoulders, elbows, and wrists.

exercises.name: Zercher Squat
instructions: Set the bar in the rack just below elbow height and hook it in the crooks of your elbows.
Keep the elbows close together, pull the bar into your body, stand it up, and step back.
Brace and squat down between the knees as deep as you can with a straight back.
Drive up through the whole foot, keeping the chest tall and the bar tight to the body.
exercises.formCue: Hug the bar in and stay tall.
exercises.commonMistakes: Letting the back round as the bar pulls forward, or going heavy before the elbows have adapted.
exercises.beginnerModification: Use a goblet squat, or wrap the bar in a pad and start with light loads.
exercises.whyThisMatters: The front-loaded position builds the trunk and upper back along with the legs.

exercises.name: One-and-a-Quarter Squat
instructions: Squat down under control to your full depth.
Without bouncing, rise only to just below parallel while keeping the legs and glutes tight.
Sink back to the bottom again.
Stand all the way up to finish one rep.
exercises.commonMistakes: Bouncing out of the bottom, or coming up too high on the quarter rep.
exercises.beginnerModification: Do the same pattern with a goblet squat or an empty bar.
exercises.whyThisMatters: The extra trip through the bottom builds leg strength and control where squats are usually lost.

exercises.name: Paused Bench Press
instructions: Lie back, pinch the shoulder blades together and down, set a slight arch, and plant the feet.
Unrack and lower the bar under control to the lower chest.
Hold the bar still on the chest for a full second while staying tight.
Press up and slightly back toward the shoulders until the elbows lock.
exercises.commonMistakes: Relaxing on the chest so the bar sinks, or lifting the hips off the bench to start the press.
exercises.beginnerModification: Use a lighter load with a short count, or pause a dumbbell bench press.
exercises.whyThisMatters: A motionless pause is how the bench is judged in competition and it builds honest strength off the chest.

exercises.name: Larsen Press
instructions: Set up as you would for your normal bench press with the shoulder blades pinched back and down.
Unrack the bar, then straighten the legs and hold the feet just off the floor.
Lower the bar under control to the lower chest.
Press back to lockout while the legs stay off the floor and the body stays still on the bench.
exercises.formCue: Legs out, upper back locked into the bench.
exercises.commonMistakes: Wobbling on the bench because the upper back is loose, or loading it like a normal bench press.
exercises.beginnerModification: Bench with the knees bent and feet resting on the bench before taking the legs out straight.
exercises.whyThisMatters: Taking leg drive away makes the chest, shoulders, and triceps do all the pressing.

exercises.name: Floor Press
instructions: Lie on the floor under a bar set low in the rack, knees bent, and take an overhand grip.
Unrack and hold the bar over the lower chest with the arms straight.
Lower until the backs of the upper arms rest fully on the floor.
Pause briefly, then press back up to lockout.
exercises.formCue: Arms settle on the floor, then press.
exercises.commonMistakes: Slamming the elbows into the floor, or bouncing off it to start the press.
exercises.beginnerModification: Use dumbbells on the floor so each arm can settle at its own pace.
exercises.whyThisMatters: The shortened range builds lockout strength with little stress at the bottom of the press.

exercises.name: Incline Barbell Bench Press
instructions: Set the bench to a low incline, lie back, and grip the bar slightly wider than the shoulders.
Unrack and bring the bar over the upper chest with the arms straight.
Lower under control to the upper chest.
Press up until the arms are fully extended.
exercises.formCue: Bar to the upper chest, elbows under the bar.
exercises.commonMistakes: Setting the bench too steep so it turns into a shoulder press, or bouncing the bar off the chest.
exercises.beginnerModification: Use the incline dumbbell press with a light load.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It builds the upper chest and shoulders and supports both the bench press and the overhead press.

exercises.name: Board Press
instructions: Lie on the bench and have a partner hold a board on your chest, or strap one in place.
Take your bench grip and unrack the bar.
Lower under control until the bar touches the board while the upper body stays tight.
Press back to lockout with a controlled, fast drive.
exercises.formCue: Touch the board, do not sink into it.
exercises.commonMistakes: Letting the bar crash into the board, or relaxing so the board shifts.
exercises.beginnerModification: Use the floor press, which shortens the range without a partner.
exercises.whyThisMatters: The shortened range lets you train the top half of the press with heavier loads.

exercises.name: Deficit Deadlift
instructions: Stand on a plate or low platform with the loaded bar over the middle of the feet.
Bend down and grip the bar, set the back flat, and pull the slack out of the bar.
Push the floor away and lift by extending the knees and hips together.
Stand fully upright, then lower the bar under control along the legs.
exercises.formCue: Stay over the bar and push the floor away.
exercises.commonMistakes: Using a platform so tall the lower back rounds, or letting the hips rise before the bar moves.
exercises.beginnerModification: Pull from the floor, or use a very small deficit with a light load.
exercises.whyThisMatters: The longer pull builds strength in the first part of the lift off the floor.

exercises.name: Pause Deadlift
instructions: Set up with the bar over the middle of the foot, grip it, breathe in, and brace.
Lift the bar a few centimetres off the floor and stop.
Hold that position for one to three seconds with the bar close and the back flat.
Finish the pull to a full stand, then lower the bar under control.
exercises.formCue: Hold your position, bar against the legs.
exercises.commonMistakes: Letting the bar drift forward during the hold, or pausing so briefly it does not count.
exercises.beginnerModification: Use a light load and a one-second pause until you can hold still.
exercises.whyThisMatters: The hold teaches a strong, balanced position at the point where many deadlifts go wrong.

exercises.name: Stiff-Leg Deadlift
instructions: Stand tall holding the bar with an overhand grip, feet about hip width.
Keep the knees nearly straight and the back flat, and bend at the hips to lower the bar.
Stop when the hamstrings are tight and before the lower back starts to round.
Extend the hips to stand back up.
exercises.formCue: Hips back, back flat, feel the hamstrings.
exercises.commonMistakes: Rounding the lower back to reach further, or bending the knees until it becomes a regular deadlift.
exercises.beginnerModification: Use the Romanian deadlift with a soft knee bend and a shorter range.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It loads the hamstrings at long length, which supports every pull from the floor.

exercises.name: Good Morning
instructions: Set the bar on your back as you would for a back squat and brace the trunk.
Unlock the knees slightly and push the hips back, lowering the chest under control.
Keep the back flat and the weight over the whole foot as far down as you can hold position.
Drive the hips forward to stand back up.
exercises.commonMistakes: Letting the back soften at the bottom, or turning it into a squat by bending the knees too much.
exercises.beginnerModification: Practice the hinge with a dowel or empty bar, or use a back extension.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It builds the back and hip strength that keeps squats and pulls from folding forward.

exercises.name: Seated Good Morning
instructions: Straddle a bench with the bar on your back as for a back squat, knees bent and feet flat in front of you.
Set the back tight and flat.
Bend forward at the hips as far as you can without the back softening.
Return to upright by extending the hips, keeping the back set the whole time.
exercises.formCue: Long spine, fold at the hips.
exercises.commonMistakes: Rounding the back to get lower, or loading it like a squat.
exercises.beginnerModification: Use an empty bar or a dowel and a shorter range.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It trains the back to hold its position with light loads and little stress on the legs.

exercises.name: Pendlay Row
exercises.musclesWorked: Lats, mid and upper back, rear delts, biceps
instructions: Stand over the bar, hinge at the hips with the knees bent until the trunk is close to horizontal, and take a shoulder-width overhand grip.
Brace the trunk the way you would for a pull from the floor.
Row the bar to the abdomen and squeeze the shoulder blades together at the top.
Lower the bar until it rests on the floor, then reset before the next rep.
exercises.formCue: Chest down, pull to the belt, back to the floor.
exercises.commonMistakes: Standing up with each rep so the hips do the work, or not letting the bar settle on the floor.
exercises.beginnerModification: Lower the load, or use a chest-supported row to learn the pull without holding the hinge.
exercises.whyThisMatters: Each rep starts from a dead stop, so the upper back does the work instead of momentum.
